articleSummary: Psittacosis (Chlamydia psittaci) is a zoonotic respiratory infection transmitted to humans from parrots, pigeons, and other birds via aerosols from droppings, urine, or feathers. Incubation is 5–14 days; symptoms range from fever and headache to pneumonia, with possible progression to severe pneumonia, ARDS, or neurologic effects. In Beijing (2023–2024), 64 cases were reported, 45 in 2024 across 11 districts, many with bird-keeping histories. Other Chinese areas—Guizhou, Nanjing, Huai’an, Wuhan, Shaoxing, Hangzhou—have reported cases. Notable outbreaks include two Beijing cases linked to pet parrots and an Anhui instance where four purchased parrots led to three deaths and subsequent human symptoms; a Wuhan cluster affected pigeon breeders and nearby residents through environmental contamination. Diagnosis often uses molecular methods such as mNGS; treatment relies on antibiotics like doxycycline and fluoroquinolones, with generally favorable prognosis. Preventive measures: buy birds from licensed sources, quarantine, hygienic handling, PPE, and seek veterinary or medical care when exposure occurs.

articleSummary: Warmer winters and earlier springs have accelerated Northward movement of Aedes albopictus in China, raising the risk of dengue and chikungunya—referred to as the 'double heat.' Guangdong saw a chikungunya outbreak in 2025; dengue and chikungunya share similar spread. articleSummary: As of 2026-04-03, Liz Way’s The Great Flood, Epidemics, and War... The End of Civilization Was Another Beginning argues that apocalypses are catalysts for resilience and renewal, not absolute endings. Drawing on archaeology and latest research, it links sea-level rise, drought, famine, and epidemics to cycles of collapse and reinvention. Harappa in the Indus Valley faced drought, reduced river flows, and disease-fueled violence as urban life strained. Maya collapse between 800–1100 CE yielded a smaller, more egalitarian and flexible mode of living. The 1492 Columbian encounter framed a modern apocalypse: European conquest of the Aztec, intensified by violence, social hierarchy, and epidemic outbreaks, with slavery and Caribbean sugar plantations deepening devastation. Neanderthals’ admixture with Homo sapiens is presented as a hopeful element in humanity’s mosaic. The work offers a sobering yet uplifting view that apocalypses inaugurate new beginnings and renewed civilization.

articleSummary: Chikungunya outbreak intensifies in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, with Dourados as the epicenter reporting 5 deaths, 1,198 confirmed cases and nearly 3,000 probable cases. The CRF-MS (Conselho Regional de Farmácia de Mato Grosso do Sul) launches a Saturday drive-thru to collect mosquito repellents to aid underserved communities, especially indigenous villages Bororó and Jaguapiru. The public health campaign aims to mobilize donations under the slogan 'Your solidarity saves lives and fights chikungunya,' sending repellents to affected areas. A prior delivery of 328 repellents to Indigenous communities in Dourados occurred on Friday, with another shipment planned. The drive-thru is on Saturday, April 4, 2026, from 7:30 to 12:00 at CRF-MS headquarters, Rua Rodolfo José Pinho, 66, Jardim São Bento, Campo Grande. Donations of repellents purchased at pharmacies are welcome.

articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) spills into China from Russia, with outbreaks in China’s northwestern border region adjoining Kazakhstan, Mongolia, and Russia. articleHeadline: Health minister pushes for campaign against dengue
articleSummary: Punjab health minister Dr Balbir Singh launched the 'Har Shukarvaar Dengue Te Vaar' campaign as a mass movement with students and teachers identifying mosquito breeding sites such as stagnant water in coolers and pots. A One Health approach links dengue, malaria, chikungunya, rabies and leptospirosis. Diagnostics expanded: free dengue/chikungunya ELISA at 47 Sentinel Surveillance Hospitals; malaria RDT and dengue testing at clinics. Dengue cases declined from 23,389 in 2021 to 4,981 in 2025; deaths fell from 55 to 8. In 2025, 42% of cases were rural, prompting fogging, larvicidal spraying in village ponds. Rabies vaccines available at 746 government facilities; district-level animal birth-control facilities target 70% herd immunity. IHIP enables real-time reporting; private practitioners urged to report notifiable diseases. 100% chlorination and regular drinking-water sampling to prevent hepatitis A/E, diarrhoea and cholera. Leptospirosis outbreak at Hazara Singh Wala, Ferozepur; SOPs planned. Punjab aims for a disease-free 2026.

articleSummary: As China enters influenza peak season with cooler weather, Dr. Hang Liangwen of the Thoracic Medicine department at China Medical University Affiliated Hospital warns that thick sputum can cause pneumonia and bacterial infection, potentially causing sepsis or death if unaddressed. Influenza features more sputum and high fever than common colds, and mucus accumulation worsens chest tightness. Deep-seated sputum is the core problem; suction devices only clear mucus from surface secretions. Effective relief requires appropriate medications; the new-generation expectorant capsules disrupt disulfide bonds in mucus to thin sputum, improving clearance, antibiotic penetration, and antioxidant effects. Do not rely on cough suppressants. Daily hydration and infection control help reduce sputum production. Vaccination is key: influenza, pneumococcal, COVID-19, and RSV vaccines are advised, especially for the elderly and chronic diseases such as COPD and asthma; caregivers should be vaccinated too. Early evaluation (X-ray, lung function, sputum culture) if cough lasts over two weeks.

The samples were secured and handed to the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock for analysis, with health authorities involved. The case rekindles debate on high-containment lab controls, as Unicamp conducts an internal biosafety review and investigators seek motives and potential others.
notes: 本イベントは感染症の発生・流行ではなく、BSL-3ラボからのサンプル盗難・無断持ち出し事件。当局がサンプルの全回収と外部曝露リスクなしを確認しているため、即座の感染症シグナルではない。しかし、バイオセキュリティ/バイオセーフティ管理の脆弱性が露呈した事案であり、国際的な制度議論の対象となる可能性がある。政治的・メディア関心は予想されるが、疫学的なピックアップ基準には未達。

triage_reason: WPROスクリーニング基準で異常性・重症度・流行可能性が該当し、学校での集団発生として注視する必要があるが、重症化や死亡の報告がなく、地方レベルの対応が既に開始されているため現段階ではWATCHとする。
articleHeadlineTranslated: Dak Lak records an outbreak of mumps at a primary school.
articleHeadline: Đắk Lắk ghi nhận một ổ dịch quai bị tại một trường tiểu học
articleSummary: Nine students from Pham Hong Thai Primary School in Cu Pông Commune, Krông Búk District, Dak Lak Province, Vietnam were diagnosed with mumps over two days as of 4 April 2026. On 3 April 2026, health authorities detected multiple suspected cases in Cu Pông, with infections spread across five classes from grades 1–3, all within the same school. Affected children presented fever, parotid gland swelling, difficulty chewing or swallowing, and fatigue; no severe complications have been reported. Transmission risk is high due to close-contact school settings. Krông Búk District Health Center has initiated outbreak control measures, including intensified public awareness campaigns and disinfection of the entire school campus; coordination with the school includes cleaning classrooms, toys, and desks to curb further spread.
notes: 学校での限局的な集団発生（9名、1つの学校）。重症例なし。当局による制御措置（清掃、啓発キャンペーン）が既に開始されている。ベトナムは予防接種率が高く、大規模流行への懸念は低い。今後の集団発生規模拡大を注視。
